But walking through the real escrow.mjs/lock.mjs mechanics this session reveals it does NOT close a distinct, equally realistic IN-PROCESS exception scenario: settleBody (escrow.mjs lines 124-140) has no try/catch around waitForTransactionReceipt, which runs AFTER /settle already succeeded; an exception here propagates uncaught through withGigLock's own try/finally (lock.mjs lines 203-208), releasing the lock CLEANLY (not stale) -- so the next caller takes the normal fast-path acquisition, never the stale-reclaim path reconcileProvisionalDisbursement is exclusively scoped to.
